inputs: Published Enigma I rotor I–V wiring and reflector B wiring
expected: All five rotors and the reflector are permutations; reflector B is a fixed-point-free involution
limitations: Checks published wiring properties only; it does not verify historical provenance beyond the cited table.

inputs: Enigma I, rotors I-II-III, reflector B, rings AAA, start AAA, no plugboard; AAAAA and BDZGO
expected: AAAAA encrypts to BDZGO and BDZGO encrypts back to AAAAA
limitations: One public simulator check vector; it is not an official historical key-sheet or message.

inputs: All 26³ start positions of Enigma I with rotors I-II-III, rings AAA, reflector B, no plugboard; all 26 letters
expected: 456,976 letter-level mappings (17,576 start positions × 26 letters): zero fixed points and zero involution failures
limitations: A finite structural check for one rotor order and one reflector; it is not a search over all keys.

inputs: Rotors III-II-I, start A-D-O; then the cycle from AAA
expected: Sequence ADO, ADP, ADQ, AER, BFS, BFT, BFU; 16,900-state cycle from AAA and a 16,926-state image of the step map over all 26³ positions
limitations: Reproduces the pawl model; 16,900 is the cycle length and 16,926 is the reachable-setting image, not the same quantity. Source wording differs and is recorded in the article.

inputs: 60 rotor orders, 16,926 reachable settings, 26×26 ring factors, 10 plugboard cables; early six rotor orders
limitations: Arithmetic under declared assumptions; nominal key-space products are not a security measure.

inputs: Ciphertext BDZGO and crib HELLO; compare same-position letters
expected: Exactly one of five alignments is impossible by no-self-encryption (the final O/O position)
limitations: A hand-checkable no-self-encryption example, not a full crib attack or Bombe search.

inputs: Enigma I I-II-III, ring and start shifted together by 0, 1, 5 and 13; 5-letter and 40-letter messages
expected: All four configurations encrypt AAAAA to BDZGO; for 40 A’s, AAA and BBB agree for 20 letters and diverge at position 21
limitations: Demonstrates the p−r offset relation for one rotor order; it does not claim all ring settings are security-equivalent.
